findings.claim: The repair-installed device_notes universal ('its structured refs carry the mandated dual-cite qualifier') is false: boundary_rationale still carries one bare offset-zone coordinate with no dual/qualifier.
findings.evidence: boundary_rationale reads "...מַֽה תֶּחֱזוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1, byte tier) 'why do you gaze at the Shulammite'..." — this oshb:Song.7.1 citation carries no '= web:' pair and no '(WEB N:N)' qualifier, unlike every other oshb:Song.7.x / web:Song.7.x citation in the row (5 other instances, all correctly dual-qualified, hand-verified field-by-field across boundary_rationale, boundary_evidence_refs, strongest_rejected_alternative and device_notes). Per the OFFSET-ZONE RULE (Tier-0), any oshb: ref touching MT ch 7 must carry an explicit dual. citation_sweep.py's offset-zone disclosure arm only iterates boundary_evidence_refs (source-verified at citation_sweep.py lines 138 and 213-222), so this prose-field bare ref is invisible to the machine suite and the row's own new universal claim in device_notes goes unchecked by it.

findings.claim: device_notes misidentifies the Hebrew word carrying the oath root at the row's own back seam: it names the word meaning 'that thus' as the form that 'repeats the oath root', when the oath root שבע is actually carried by the immediately following word.
findings.evidence: device_notes: "at the back seam, שֶׁכָּ֖כָה (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) repeats the oath root immediately across this row's own closing verse, the daughters quoting it back". Source oshb:Song.5.9 (verse_map_oshb.json, byte tier) is "מַה דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים מַה דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד שֶׁכָּ֖כָה הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ" — the word cited, שֶׁכָּ֖כָה, is the relative 'she-' + 'kakha' ('that thus'), which carries no שבע root; the actual oath-root verb is the following word, הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ ('you have adjured us'). The sibling row P02-003's repair, covering the same verse and the same front-seam oath-recurrence point, correctly cites הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (present verbatim in P02-003's boundary_rationale, byte-confirmed) as the oath-root/plural-speaker form; שֶׁכָּ֖כָה does not appear there. This is exactly the toolkit's own flagged hazard ('שבע oath-only homograph ... name root AND speech role') — the wrong word was spliced as the root-bearing token.

findings.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative cites 'the strategy's own hybrid rule' as the ground for holding the unit whole — a strategy-file citation barred from row prose by REGISTER PURGE, the same defect class this repair wave explicitly struck from sibling rows P02-021 and P02-022 in the same cycle but missed here.
findings.evidence: strongest_rejected_alternative: "Splitting 6:1 (question) from 6:2-3 (answer plus refrain) into two rows was considered, but the exchange is verse-scale and the strategy's own hybrid rule holds this daughters-question-with-answer zone whole rather than atomizing it." Contrast P02-021's repaired strongest_rejected_alternative, which argues the person-form seam from bytes alone with no strategy citation, and P02-022's, which likewise argues hold-whole only from the 2fs/2ms minimal pair and the vocative — both had an identical 'the strategy's own X' / 'the strategy names X' construction removed by this same phase-1 wave per their own remedy text ('a strategy-file citation barred from row prose by the register rule; re-argue the hold-whole ground from the verses themselves'). P02-005's boundary_rationale itself argues the daughters' plural forms and the mutual-belonging shape from bytes independently, so the barred sentence is not load-bearing for the boundary conclusion, but it remains barred content left in the row.

findings.claim: device_notes' front-seam address-vocabulary disclosure names the chain as continuing from oshb:Song.4.9, 4.10 and 4.12 into 5:2, omitting the immediately adjacent occurrence at oshb:Song.5.1 (the row's own front-seam neighbor, P02-001), which the toolkit's bride-epithet inventory and P02-001's own repaired device_notes both place in the same 5-verse chain.
findings.evidence: P02-002 device_notes: "the man's address vocabulary פִּתְחִי לִ֞י אֲחֹתִ֤י רַעְיָתִי֙ (oshb:Song.5.2, byte tier) continues the bride-epithet chain from oshb:Song.4.9, 4.10 and 4.12" — skips 5:1. P02-001 device_notes (same repair wave, front-seam neighbor row) already discloses "אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ (oshb:Song.5.1, byte tier) ... the bride-epithet form (sweep: 5 verses, word-bound)" i.e. MT 4:9, 4:10, 4:12, 5:1, 5:2 per the toolkit device inventory ('bride-epithet form: 5 verses, word-bound, MT 4:9, 4:10, 4:12, 5:1, 5:2'). Low confidence: the omission may be a deliberate role-split (5:1's kallah-pairing vs. 5:2's rayati-pairing use of achoti) rather than an oversight, but as worded it reads as skipping the nearest link in the very chain it is disclosing across the seam it shares with P02-001.
